nodes.text: INSTANT · ON-DEVICE AI The provided document is a summary of the U.S. Constitution , specifically focusing on its provisions regarding political structure, executive power, and legislative procedures. Main Points: • Legislative Body: The constitution establishes a bicameral legislature with the House of Representatives (chosen every second year) and the Senate (elected by state legislatures for six-year terms). Senators serve one vote each; the President has no such power over impeachment or public office removals. • Executive Power: The President signs bills but can return them with objections if not approved, requiring a two-thirds vote in both houses to become law before reconsideration. • Financial and Diplomatic Powers: No State may enter treaties/Alliances, coin money, or issue credit notes without Congressional consent; no State may lay duties or taxes on imports/exports without consent. • Diplomatic Restrictions: No State may keep troops/ships of war unless invaded or in immediate danger. The President is elected for four-year terms from the states' electors (majority vote, age 14+), and Vice President is chosen by a tie between two or more equal candidates. • Constitutional Rights: Article 4 guarantees every State a Republican Form of Government against domestic violence upon application; Article 5 allows amendments only if two-thirds consent in either house or three-fourths of the states, excluding prior amendment affecting Article I clause one.
